chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He (peace be upon him) was saying: 'When one of you wears his sandal, let him wear the right one before the left, and when he takes it off, let him take off the left one before the right one.'
ai.seo_question: What is the proper order for putting on and taking off shoes according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the specific ritual etiquette (adab) for footwear, emphasizing the precedence of the right side during application and the left during removal, a practice rooted in the Prophet’s tradition. In Shia scholarship, this is viewed not merely as hygiene but as an act of imitating the divine order, where the right symbolizes strength and blessing, while the structured removal ensures dignity and cleanliness. It serves as a microcosm of the broader Islamic principle of infusing daily mundane actions with spiritual mindfulness.

en.hubeali:
A number or our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn Al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>
was saying: ‘Whenever one of you wears his sandals, so let him wear the right before the left, and when he takes them off, so let him take-off the left before the right’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ash‘ariy from ibn al-Qaddah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When one of you wears his shoes he must wear on the right foot first then the left foot, when taking off you should remove from the left before the right.’”
